intro: SBI PO (2026-27 cycle: Advertisement CRPD/PO/2026-27/09, 1,500 vacancies) runs in three phases: a 100-question Prelims, a Mains with a 170-question objective paper plus a 30-mark descriptive paper, and a Phase-III of psychometric test, group exercise and interview. The final merit gives 75 percent weight to the Mains and 25 percent to group exercise and interview.
note: The official advertisement names the tests and sections (with question counts, marks and timing) but does not enumerate a topic-wise syllabus. The topics below are the conventional scope of each named section as tested in recent SBI and IBPS papers; treat them as a study map, not an official list, and confirm anything specific to a cycle from the official advertisement and information handouts.

sections.name: English Language
topics: Fill in the blanks (single and double)
Match the column and multiple-fill patterns
sections.tip: The Prelims is 100 questions, 100 marks and 1 hour, with a 20-minute timer on each section (English 40, Quant 30, Reasoning 30).

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
topics: Data interpretation: tables, bar charts, line graphs, pie charts, caselets, missing data
Quantity comparison (Quantity I/II) and data sufficiency
Percentage, ratio and proportion, average, ages
Time and work, pipes and cisterns
Time, speed and distance; boats and streams; trains
Number series (missing and wrong number) and simplification/approximation

sections.name: Reasoning Ability
topics: Puzzles and seating arrangement (linear, circular, floor-based, scheduling, box, tabular)

sections.name: General/Economy/Banking Awareness
topics: Current affairs of roughly the last six months
RBI policy, circulars and monetary matters
sections.tip: The advertisement names the test without itemising topics; banking, economy and finance news dominate recent papers.

sections.name: Data Analysis & Interpretation
topics: Data interpretation: tables, bar charts, line graphs, pie charts, radar charts, caselets, missing data
Quantity comparison (Quantity I/II) and data sufficiency
Arithmetic: percentage, ratio, average, interest, profit and loss, time and work, time, speed and distance, mixtures and alligations, partnership
sections.tip: The Mains paper is named Data Analysis & Interpretation and carries 60 marks from just 30 questions (2 marks each), so DI sets and high-mark arithmetic dominate; the Prelims quant section is broader and more speed-driven.

sections.name: Reasoning & Computer Aptitude
topics: Statement and assumption, statement and conclusion, statement and course of action
Logical reasoning: cause and effect, arguments, inference
Coding and decoding, blood relations, direction and distance, order and ranking
Flowchart and logic-based computer reasoning questions
sections.tip: In the Mains this test is combined with computer aptitude and carries 60 marks from 40 questions; expect multi-variable puzzles, input-output and statement-based questions at higher difficulty than the Prelims.

sections.name: English Language
topics: Fill in the blanks (single and double)
Match the column and multiple-fill patterns
sections.tip: In the Mains the English test carries only 20 marks across 40 questions (0.5 mark each), so speed matters more than depth there. The descriptive paper that follows the objective test is where written English is scored in earnest: 3 questions for 30 marks in 30 minutes (email writing, situation analysis, and report writing or precis writing).

sections.name: Computer Aptitude
topics: Banking technology: core banking, ATM, UPI, NEFT/RTGS/IMPS, digital payment systems
Cyber security and internet safety basics
Flowchart and logic-based computer reasoning questions
sections.tip: There is no separate computer section: computer aptitude is tested inside the Mains Reasoning & Computer Aptitude test (often as flowchart and logic questions), and the Prelims has no computer questions. The advertisement does not break the list down further.
